parts.markdown:
Use our free **Alaska paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare, Alaska unemployment insurance contributions and other payroll deductions.

Alaska does not impose an individual state income tax on employment earnings, which distinguishes it from most US states. However, federal taxes and certain state payroll contributions can still reduce the amount you receive on payday.

Whether you work in Anchorage, Fairbanks, Juneau or a remote Alaskan community, understanding your net earnings can help you evaluate job opportunities and manage the cost of living.

## How to Use the Alaska Paycheck Calculator

If your pay stub lists Alaska employee unemployment insurance, include the amount under other deductions. Enter each deduction once.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage before taxes and deductions.

Choose your pay frequency, including weekly, biweekly, semimonthly or monthly payments.

Enter federal income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Add retirement contributions, health insurance premiums and other employee deductions.

If you have already earned income during the current calendar year, enter your year-to-date taxable wages to improve the accuracy of the Social Security estimate.

Review the results to see your estimated gross pay, individual deductions and net paycheck.

You can also compare different salary offers by changing your income and benefit information.

## Alaska Payroll Taxes in 2026

Although Alaska has no individual state income tax, employees may still face several payroll deductions.

The [Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development](https://labor.alaska.gov/estax/2026-experience-rates.html) publishes official unemployment insurance rates and annual taxable wage limits.

## Does Alaska Have State Income Tax?

Alaska does not impose an individual state income tax on employment earnings.

For employees relocating from states with significant individual income taxes, this can improve take-home pay when other circumstances remain unchanged.

However, living in a state without individual income tax does not automatically mean that every worker has more disposable income.

Federal income tax remains applicable. Housing, groceries, transportation, heating and insurance costs can also influence the financial benefits of living in Alaska.

Local governments may collect other types of taxes, including sales and property taxes, which can affect household expenses without appearing as ordinary state income tax withholding on your paycheck.

The Alaska paycheck calculator separates the absence of state income tax from other applicable deductions.

## Alaska Employee Unemployment Insurance Contributions

Alaska is among the states that collect unemployment insurance contributions directly from covered employees.

For 2026, the employee contribution rate is 0.50% of covered wages, subject to an annual taxable wage base of $54,200.

The maximum standard annual contribution is therefore:

$54,200 × 0.005 = $271

Your employer's unemployment insurance contribution is separate and should not automatically be deducted from your paycheck.

The employee contribution supports Alaska's unemployment insurance system, which provides benefits to qualifying workers experiencing unemployment.

## How the Annual Unemployment Insurance Limit Works

Suppose you have already earned $53,000 in covered wages during 2026 and receive another paycheck containing $2,000 in covered earnings.

Only $1,200 remains below the $54,200 wage ceiling.

The employee contribution for that paycheck would be:

$1,200 × 0.005 = $6

Applying the contribution rate to the entire $2,000 would incorrectly produce a $10 deduction.

This demonstrates why year-to-date earnings are an important calculator input.

Employees earning above the annual limit may notice a small increase in take-home pay later in the calendar year when unemployment insurance contributions stop.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Alaska Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Alaska residents are generally subject to federal income tax even though their state does not impose individual income tax.

Your employer calculates federal withholding using your taxable earnings, filing status, pay frequency and Form W-4 information.

The federal withholding methodology is available in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security.

For 2026, the annual taxable wage limit is $184,500.

Some public-sector employees may participate in alternative retirement arrangements and have different Social Security coverage. Check your employment terms before assuming that ordinary Social Security withholding applies.

### Medicare

The standard Medicare employee contribution is 1.45% of covered earnings.

An additional 0.9% generally applies through employer withholding once Medicare wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

The [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) explains these federal payroll contribution requirements.

Your actual take-home pay depends on your federal withholding elections and benefit deductions.

## Alaska Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employment is common across Alaska's transportation, tourism, construction, fishing and natural resource industries.

Suppose an hourly worker earns $30 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus eight qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$30 × 40 = $1,200

Overtime earnings:

$30 × 1.5 × 8 = $360

Total gross earnings:

$1,560

Applicable federal taxes and Alaska unemployment insurance contributions are then calculated using the relevant taxable wage amounts.

Alaska generally requires qualifying overtime compensation for hours worked beyond eight in a day or 40 in a week, subject to exemptions and applicable employment arrangements.

Consult the [Alaska Wage and Hour Administration](https://labor.alaska.gov/lss/whhome.htm) before estimating overtime for specialized occupations or alternative work schedules.

## Seasonal Employment and Alaska Paychecks

Many Alaska industries experience significant seasonal changes in employment demand.

Tourism, commercial fishing and construction workers may earn substantial income during certain months and considerably less during others.

A calculator that estimates annual income from one unusually large paycheck may therefore produce a misleading annual projection.

For seasonal employment, estimate your total annual income separately rather than assuming your current earnings will continue at the same rate throughout the year.

Also consider unpaid periods between contracts, travel expenses and employer-provided accommodation when evaluating employment opportunities.

## Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend and Take-Home Pay

The Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend, commonly known as the PFD, is separate from ordinary employment earnings.

Eligible residents may receive an annual dividend when they meet applicable program requirements.

The payment amount varies by year and eligibility is not automatic.

A PFD payment is generally subject to federal income tax, even though Alaska does not impose individual state income tax.

Do not add an assumed dividend payment to your regular paycheck when calculating your employment earnings.

Visit the official [Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend website](https://pfd.alaska.gov/) to review eligibility, application requirements and payment information.

## Planning Your Budget Around Alaska Take-Home Income

Alaska's geography can create significant differences in living expenses between communities.

Heating, groceries, transportation and housing may cost considerably more in remote locations than in larger cities.

Before accepting a position, compare estimated net earnings alongside accommodation benefits, transportation allowances and expected living expenses.

Use our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) to establish a savings target, particularly if your employment is seasonal or your income fluctuates.

A higher salary is most valuable when it produces a meaningful improvement in your remaining income after essential household expenses.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Alaska deduct state income tax from paychecks?

No. Alaska does not impose an individual state income tax on wages. Federal income tax, applicable payroll contributions and other employee deductions may still reduce your paycheck.

### What is the Alaska unemployment insurance deduction in 2026?

The standard employee contribution is 0.50% of covered earnings up to $54,200 annually, producing a maximum standard annual employee contribution of $271.

### Is the Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend included in my paycheck?

No. The Permanent Fund Dividend is a separate payment for qualifying residents and is not part of ordinary employment payroll.
